chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Cue sheets for a leading drummer
summary: As leader he wrote cue sheets of intros, choruses and tags rather than full drum parts, except for rock-and-roll acts at the Regal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did he always write drummer parts for you?
With me? They -- a lot of times, on account of conducting and leading the band and all of that, I had more or less a guide. Like, what I would do, --

Yeah, a cue sheet. Whatever the introduction was, if I had to write up a four-bar introduction, I would do that. Then I'd write so many choruses, four choruses, so-and-so, eight bar tag, so-and-so, this type of a thing. And this gave me the freedom of playing, unless it was an act that required you to read the part, because I know once I had to play a thing for one of the rock and roll singers at the Regal. And there was a tune, and I had to read this thing, because of the way that the licks and things were to be, and it was all synchronized right with the arrangements and had to be that way. Yeah.
